metadata.title: Dafke UI
metadata.description: A fully custom React component library based on the Dafke UI design. No shadcn, no Radix, no external UI dependencies.

home.titleLine2: built on the Dafke UI design.
home.intro: Works like shadcn — same composition, same copy-paste approach — but without a single line of code from shadcn, Radix or any other UI library. Everything lives in your own repo.
home.allDescription: From button to command palette, from table to donut chart.

zeroDeps.title: Zero UI dependencies
zeroDeps.text: No shadcn, no Radix, no Headless UI. Every component — focus trap, positioning and keyboard navigation included — is written right here.

tokens.title: Every color from one source
tokens.text: Every color, radius and shadow comes from the Dafke UI design. Components use tokens only, never a hardcoded hex.

copyPaste.title: Copy-paste, your code
copyPaste.text: Just like shadcn: `npx dafke-ui add button` copies the source into your project. You own the components and change them whenever you like.

theme.title: Light and dark
theme.text: One ThemeProvider, two complete palettes. Everything follows along, charts and overlays included.

intro.lead: A React component library of our own, built from the Dafke UI design. The API feels like shadcn — composition with sub-components, asChild, controlled and uncontrolled — but there is not a single line of external UI code in it. No shadcn, no Radix, no Headless UI, no cva, no clsx: everything lives in packages/ui/src.
intro.buildDesc: The library grows step by step. Each step adds components and their docs.
intro.getComponentsText: All on the same tokens, and more arrive with every step.
intro.getPrimitivesText: cn(), variants(), Slot and hooks — written here.
intro.getA11yText: ARIA roles, keyboard navigation and visible focus on every interactive component.
intro.rule1Title: Every colour comes from the Dafke UI design
intro.rule1Body: Components use CSS variables only (var(--accent), var(--surface), …). Want to recolour? Change tokens.css and the whole library follows.
intro.rule2Body: Every class starts with lui-, so nothing collides with existing CSS in your projects.
intro.rule3Body: Tailwind v4 provides the reset and the utilities for your own markup. The components themselves are plain CSS classes — no utility soup, fully editable.

install.title: Installation
install.lead: Dafke UI works in any React project with a bundler (Next.js, Vite, Remix). Two ways: copy components with the CLI, or use the monorepo directly.
install.s1Text: This is the documentation site you are looking at, with all the source files next to it.
install.s1Structure: Structure: packages/ui (the library), packages/cli (the add CLI), apps/docs (this site) and registry/ (generated JSON).
install.s2Title: 2 · Put components into an existing project
install.s2Init: init creates dafke-ui.json with your paths and copies the shared files (tokens, base CSS, cn(), variants(), Slot, Portal, hooks and the icon set).
install.npmBody: Link the CLI once from this monorepo with cd packages/cli && npm link. After that dafke-ui init works in every project on your machine and the CLI finds the registry by itself. Or pass a path or URL with --registry, for example the raw URL of registry/index.json on GitHub.
install.s2Index: The CLI also maintains components/ui/index.ts, so you import everything through @/components/ui. Internal helpers (cn, hooks, anchor …) are deliberately left out; import those directly, e.g. @/components/ui/cn.
install.s2Update: update pulls the latest version of everything already in your project and installs the components that have been added to the registry since. Files you changed yourself stay as they are — they are skipped unless you pass --force. Preview what would happen with --dry-run, or stick to what you have with --only-installed. The CLI keeps dafke-ui.lock.json for this; commit that file.
install.s3Text: Import one stylesheet into your global CSS. The order does not matter; everything uses cascade-free classes.
install.twBody: The components do not need Tailwind — they use their own lui- classes. Tailwind v4 is there only for the reset and for utilities in your own markup. If you do use Tailwind, also import tailwind.css: the same tokens then exist as utilities (bg-accent, rounded-lg). Without Tailwind, leave that file out.
install.s4Text: Two providers go once at the top of your app: theme and notifications.
install.fontsText: The design uses Hanken Grotesk for text and JetBrains Mono for code. Load them from Google Fonts, or change --font and --mono in tokens.css.
install.req3: A bundler that handles CSS imports (Next.js, Vite, …)
install.req4: No UI or utility library at all — deliberately left out

theming.title: Theme & tokens
theming.lead: Every colour in this library comes from one file: tokens.css. Components never write a hex value — they only use variables. Change a token and the whole UI follows, in light and dark.
theming.sourceBody: The values below are taken verbatim from the admin panel design. Need a second brand? Copy the :root block and override it under your own selector, for example [data-brand="client-x"].
theming.recolorText: Changing one variable is enough to recolour the whole library:
theming.densityText: Besides light and dark, the library has one scale knob: --density. Every height and padding is written as calc(Npx * var(--density)), so compact and roomy immediately carry through buttons, fields, tables, lists and calendars — without touching a single component.
theming.densityProvider: ThemeProvider sets data-density on <html> and remembers the choice; DensityToggle is the ready-made switch and ThemeScript restores it before the first paint.
